items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: And then they had another segment where they would play Lunceford, Kirk, Basie, Duke, Louis Jordan, the Savoy Sultans, there was another guy — what the heck, they did the song called “Who Threw the”— Doc Wheeler.

ctx.x: Now did you know who the Fletcher Henderson orchestra was at that time?

At that time? Not really. Not really. We had recordings at home — we had Paul Whiteman and Amos ‘n Andy and the Two Black Crows and a bunch of other names. We may have had something by Fletcher Henderson because we had records. See my dad, being a chauffeur, the people were always giving him records, the people he worked for. So we may have had Fletcher Henderson records. I know that I became aware of him — oh it was after my mother died. I became aware of him because we had a station in Berkeley called KRE and…

some reason or another it didn’t last as a ballroom so they eventually turned it into a skating rink and the eventually back to a bowling alley. But Krupa went over to Sweet’s. And he played Sweet’s Ballroom just that one night, I mean two nights, and on the third night I was there and he did that “Wire Brush Stomp” which was a famous recording that he did, and at the end of it he threw the brush out in the audience. Unfortunately I didn’t catch it. But he was another guy that was one of my idols.
